summary: Measured from files only (D:/UEMA_Research). The saved model is 18,131,745 parameters (fp32 storage, 73.1 MB), d_model 192, 4 transformer blocks with 8 heads, context 128 model steps; six senses are active (vision, tactile, audio, proprioception, motor, vestibular; intermind is not in the active list), each pooled to ONE 192-number token per model step, so the transformer reads 6 tokens per model step and a sequence of 768 = 6 senses x 128 model steps. Vision per body: 2 eye cameras at 256 px / 60 degrees (default eye_size 256) plus 2 fovea cameras at 288 px / 24 degrees plus 1 left-eye ring camera at 150 degrees; with 16-px patches that is 256 + 324 = 580 patches per eye, 1,160 patches (each 16x16x3 numbers) per body per render, rendered every 2 model steps (render_every 2). The planner is not a candidate enumeration: it refines ONE command per body by Adam (lr 0.1) for n_steps 20, evaluating the starting command and every update (21 forward-model evaluations, 20 backward passes through the frozen forward model), batched over the 8 bodies, once every 10 model steps (intention_every 10) once the goal ring holds 20 moments; the horizon is 1 depth under hand_target_mode wrist_relative_v1 (plan_length 1 in the last record) even though the earned licence reads 3; a separate hand descent of 20 steps runs beside it. The motor controller runs up to 4 adaptive blocks of hidden 128 (think_harder on). Worlds: 8 (--n-envs 8, each a separate process in PoolSource); one world is a supported path (--n-envs 1 -> SingleEnvSource). Batches: live training batch = 8 bodies every model step (one forward + backward + AdamW step); replay every 2 model steps on 24 windows of 129 moments (context 128 + target); imagination chain 3 forward passes every model step; synergy lesson batch 64. Replay ring: 6,000 moments per body x 8 = 48,000 moments on CPU, computed about 195 MB (tokens 110.6 MB fp16, achieved 25.0 MB, executed 22.5 MB, memory states 36.9 MB). Checkpoint: model.safetensors 73,119,988 B; optimizer.pt 138,060,045 B; runtime_state.pt 489,337,136 B (self_rehearsal 267.0 MB and self_history 195.4 MB of it); episode_state.pt.gz 621,243,950 B; latent_body/latest.pt 6,046,784 B; trajectory.jsonl 477,730,033 B; checkpoint folder 1,322,009,657 B; whole bundle 1,848,426,182 B over 289 files. Measured on the RTX 4070 laptop (README, Oct 22 2026): GPU memory peak 4,287 MB; committed memory rose 44.0 -> 73.8 GB (about 30 GB for trainer + 8 world processes); 0.41 to 0.46 model steps per second; 376 s for the 100-model-step run. The run's own last record: 0.444 model steps/s, 17.78 physics env steps/s, per-model-step time model 1,984.3 ms + env 250.4 ms (training included), peak CUDA allocation 4,213.5 MB, nvidia-smi 6,961 of 8,188 MiB. Inference-only cost is NOT measured in these files: --eval-only ("act but do not learn") exists but no throughput record for it is in the release; what can be stated from code is that inference still needs autograd, because the planner's 20 Adam updates backpropagate through the forward model every 10 model steps. Training-only costs: the per-model-step backward on 8 bodies, AdamW state (optimizer.pt 138 MB = two fp32 moments of 18.1M), the replay pass (24 x 129-moment windows every 2 model steps), the imagination chain, and the 489 MB runtime state. Port-relevant code facts: the model falls back to CPU fp32 without AMP when CUDA is absent (lem_model.py 785-800); the only CUDA-source extensions are tokenizer/modalities/vision_kernels.py (used by the Unreal path tokenizer/modalities/vision.py, not by the MIMo bridge, whose vision goes through numpy in mimo_bridge/vision_adapter.py) and lem/native_ops.py ("Pure C++ (no CUDA kernels)" but includes CUDA headers; "Falls back to pure-Python implementations if compilation fails"); pins are torch==2.6.0+cu124, mujoco==3.3.0, Python 3.13. No file in the release states MuJoCo, PyTorch or the trainer's Python running on iOS or an Apple GPU; those are open questions needing external sources.

The model-side 1,984.3 ms per model step mixes acting, planning, the live backward, replay and imagination. summary: Inventory of CUDA/NVIDIA dependencies in D:/UEMA_Research/Source/Python against the path resume.py -> mimo_bridge.train_mimo actually runs with the released command (weights/b1_continue_B1K_skip13_492800/run/command.json, --device cuda:0, 8 worlds, resume from ckpt_step_494025). RESULT: lem/native_ops.py (nvrtc-compiled CUDA kernel, nvcuda.dll D3D12 interop, at::cuda::CUDAGraph replay, raw cudaMemcpyAsync) is NOT on the released path: its only importers are lem/replay_buffer.py and lem/training_step.py, and neither is imported by mimo_bridge/train_mimo.py or mimo_bridge/lem_model.py (the only tool importing them is mimo_bridge/tools/contract_overseer.py). Its C++ source includes <cuda.h> and ATen CUDA headers unconditionally and is built with with_cuda=True, so it has no Metal build; load_native_ops() returns None without MSVC and every Python wrapper then falls back to plain torch (tensor.item(), tensor.cpu().tolist(), torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(foreach=True), loss.backward(), dst.copy_), except run_native_inference_loop, which raises. No test in the release shows the clip_grad_norm fallback bit-equal to the C++ (the C++ forms per-tensor norms, stacks them, takes the norm of the stack and clips by max_norm/(total_norm+1e-6) clamped to 1.0; the fallback calls torch's own function); treated as approximate until measured. torch.compile is only called in lem/live_test.py (Unreal path) and LITE_OVERRIDES sets torch_compile enabled False; CUDA graphs exist only in native_ops.py; GradScaler is constructed only in live_test.py. ON the released path the CUDA-specific pieces are: (1) lem_model.py:785 picks the device with `torch.cuda.is_available()` and otherwise silently falls to CPU, so "mps" is never selected; (2) lem_model.py:798-800 forces float32 and use_amp False off CUDA, while the saved receipt records precision "bf16"; (3) 8 autocast sites in lem_model.py plus heads_all_slot_path.py:514, motor_asked_change.py:471, vestibular_input_path.py:398, proprio_token.py:535 hard-code device_type "cuda" (torch 2.6.0 autocast_mode.py:261-269 warns and disables when CUDA is absent, so they become no-ops rather than MPS autocast); (4) mimo_bridge/continuation_state.py:216-218 refuses to restore a companion that carries a CUDA RNG state on a non-CUDA device ("exact continuation requires the saved execution device"), and train_mimo.py:2768 calls that restore on every resume: the released episode_state.pt.gz was written by a cuda:0 run, so a Mac resume stops there unless the port changes that rule (and then the exact random continuation of the saved run is lost); (5) acting_snapshot.py:54 calls torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all whenever the snapshot holds a CUDA state, with no device check; (6) float64 tensors created ON the model's device by features the command switches on: hand_response.py:117,138 (finger-joint servo and hand-response calibration), persistent_memory.py:344-368 buffers (persistent-memory on), self_state_integration.py:41 (self-state learn), prediction_audit.py:388 - the PyTorch MPS notes state "The MPS backend does not support torch.float64" and that such tensors "cannot be allocated or copied to MPS in the first place", so each of these must move to CPU or to float32 (float32 changes the arithmetic the receipts record, e.g. the vestibular check lists float64 among its check precisions). lem/model/attention_cap.py forces no float64 (it promotes to float32 and only computes float64 "for float64 inputs"), and the released command runs --attention-cap off, so its CappedMultiheadAttention is nn.MultiheadAttention's own forward. Guarded and harmless off CUDA: AdamW fused=(d.type=="cuda"), encoder_registry CUDA event, efference timing synchronize, train_mimo peak_vram, machine_stats, lem_model plan RNG fork. Platform facts: mujoco 3.3.0 ships macosx_11_0_arm64 and macosx_10_16_x86_64 cp313 wheels (PyPI 2025-02-27) and env.py's mujoco.GLContext picks the CGL backend on Darwin, so the 8 spawned MuJoCo worlds with offscreen eye rendering have a macOS path (untested here); torch 2.6.0 has a cp313 macosx_11_0_arm64 wheel (PyPI 2025-01-29) but README/requirements pin the cu124 index, and MPS needs macOS 15.0+ per the PyTorch sample. resume.py itself refuses to build the command on macOS: line 57 compares the saved backslash paths against DEV_ROOT + os.sep ("/" on macOS), the test fails, and line 61-62 then reports "a path of the development machine this script does not map" (reasoned from the file, not run). iOS: MuJoCo's README names prebuilt binaries for Linux, Windows and macOS only and the 3.3.0 release assets are linux/macos-universal2/windows; ExecuTorch is "PyTorch's solution for efficient AI inference on edge devices" and its training extension is "experimental and under heavy active development" with "no way yet to serialize the newly trained weights" - the released trainer (Python, 8 spawned worker processes, MuJoCo CGL rendering) has no iOS runtime; an iOS target would be an inference-only re-export, which no file in the release prepares.

findings.topic: The clip_grad_norm fallback is not shown bit-equivalent to the C++
findings.meaning_for_port: The C++ takes per-tensor norms (`torch::norm(g, norm_type)`, line 204), stacks them and takes `torch::norm(stacked, norm_type)` (207-208), then scales by max_norm/(total_norm+1e-6) clamped at 1.0. The fallback delegates to torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ with foreach=True. The release carries no test comparing the two outputs, so bit-equivalence is unmeasured; treat as approximate. The GIL-release difference (py::gil_scoped_release, lines 123, 215, 506, 528) changes timing only, not values. Irrelevant to the released MIMo path, which never imports the file.

Adam is planned." and "We don't have a way yet to serialize the newly trained weights natively in ExecuTorch". The training path is: train_mimo.main builds PoolSource (datasource.py:1936 call at train_mimo.py:1936) which spawns 8 Python worker processes with multiprocessing context "spawn" and one Pipe each (datasource.py:495-511); each worker owns one BridgeEnv and renders its two eyes (256x256), two foveae (288x288) and the ring (256 px over 150 deg) offscreen through one mujoco.GLContext per process (env.py:587-638), plus a 480 px watch-camera JPEG every model step (--live-view-every 1); the parent process runs the LemLite model on torch.device("cuda:0" if available else "cpu") (lem_model.py:785). Named shared memory (shm_writer.py, lem/action/shm.py) is Mode B (the Unreal transport) and is NOT on the training path (datasource.py:3-8, __init__.py:16-17). Windows-only code on the training path is limited to guarded branches (machine_stats.py:69-70 nvidia-smi flag, psutil in try/except, native_ops MSVC-only JIT that returns None elsewhere, CUDA vision kernels that return None without nvcc); drive-letter paths in records and the saved command are re-rooted by repo_paths.py and resume.py. MIMo's own imports on the training path are gymnasium (MujocoEnv, spaces, MujocoRenderer which imports glfw at module top), trimesh, cachetools, matplotlib.pyplot (touch.py, vision.py) and cv2 (vision.py module level); stable_baselines3 is imported only lazily inside illustrations.py and is not on the training path. macOS port: MuJoCo 3.3.0, torch 2.6.0, gymnasium and imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0 all ship macOS arm64 wheels; mujoco picks the CGL context on Darwin; multiprocessing spawn is already macOS's default; the model falls to CPU float32 unless line 785 is changed to select "mps", and MPS cannot run the float64 tensors lem_model allocates (lines 2533-2534); the live viewer tool needs mjpython. The measured RAM (committed memory rose 44.0 to 73.8 GB for trainer + 8 worlds) and 4,287 MB of graphics memory are the resource line. iOS port: Python's docs state an iOS app cannot use subprocessing, multiprocessing or inter-process communication (so PoolSource, the git/sysctl/nvidia-smi/ffmpeg subprocess calls and mujoco's own import-time sysctl call are blockers unless removed), no torch wheel exists for iOS (ExecuTorch is inference-only), MuJoCo's renderer needs OpenGL 1.5 compatibility profile with a canonical OpenGL library that MuJoCo names only for Windows, macOS and Linux, the gymnasium render module imports glfw, and every binary module must be repackaged as a framework; continuing the saved 8-body episode in one process is refused by the trainer's continuation check (train_mimo.py:1889-1890) because n_envs is part of it.

findings.topic: Python embedding rules on iOS for every binary module
findings.quote: The iOS App Store requires that _all_ binary modules in an iOS app must be dynamic libraries, contained in a framework with appropriate metadata, stored in the `Frameworks` folder of the packaged app. There can be only a single binary per framework, and there can be no executable binary material outside the `Frameworks` folder.
findings.meaning_for_port: Source: https://docs.python.org/3/using/ios.html (header Python 3.15.2), which also states "the only way you can use Python on iOS is in embedded mode" and "By default, when compiled for iOS, Python will be compiled with a minimum supported iOS version of 13.0." The release's training path imports numpy, scipy (hand_target_control.py:325 `from scipy.optimize import minimize, LinearConstraint`), torch, mujoco, trimesh/rtree, Pillow, imageio, PyYAML, safetensors, gymnasium's glfw binding and cv2/matplotlib through MIMo: each binary module needs its own framework, and torch and mujoco have no iOS builds at all (see those findings). resume.py:49 `args = [sys.executable] + saved[1:]` and :89 `return subprocess.call(args, cwd=REPO / "Source" / "Python")` launch the trainer as a second process, which the iOS docs forbid: the iOS entry point must call train_mimo.main(argv) in-process.

findings.meaning_for_port: save_ckpt writes lineage.json into the checkpoint folder and appends to a registry two levels above `out`, inside `try ... except OSError: log.warning("could not write lineage for %s", p)` (2706-2712); the episode companion is written by continuation_state.save with each worker's pickled world streamed one at a time (datasource.py:573-590 iter_world_blobs). macOS: no change. iOS: `out` must be inside the app container so that `out/../..` is writable, or the OSError branch logs a warning each save.
